title: Your First Node.js and Express Server
summary: Start a local Express application, listen on a provided port, and return the first HTTP response.

sketchBlocks.title: Node.js hosts the process; Express organizes HTTP handling

tryItExercises.title: Start a different local Express service
tryItExercises.prompt: Create an Express application named `app` and start it on port `3000` at `127.0.0.1`. Log a short ready message from the listen callback.
tryItExercises.hint: Separate creating the application from starting the listener.

help.concept: An Express server needs one application object and one local listener before routes can receive requests.
help.hint_1: Load Express first, then call it to create the application.
help.hint_2: The listener belongs after application creation and uses the provided local host and port.

tryItExercises.starterCode:
const express = require("express");

// Create the Express application below.

sourceChecks.message: Listen on the provided local host and port.

sketchBlocks.title: A route connects a method and path to response code

tryItExercises.title: Add a readiness route
tryItExercises.prompt: Keep the local Express server and add `GET /api/status`. Respond with the text `Campus API ready`.
tryItExercises.hint: Register the read route on the `app` object before the listener.

help.concept: An Express GET route pairs one path with one handler and completes the response through `res`.
help.hint_1: The route registration uses the application object and a path string.
help.hint_2: The handler receives request and response objects; only the response object needs to send this text.

quizDraft.title: Separate Node and Express responsibilities
quizDraft.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship used in this course?
quizDraft.hint: One runs the server-side JavaScript process; the other gives that process routing helpers.

help.concept: Node.js and Express have different responsibilities in a backend application.
help.hint_1: Think about which layer provides the JavaScript runtime.
help.hint_2: Then identify the layer that exposes methods such as `app.get`.

options: Node.js runs server-side JavaScript; Express organizes HTTP routes and middleware.
Express replaces JavaScript with a new programming language.
Node.js is only the JSON format returned by an API.
Express is the network address used by localhost.

quizDraft.title: Identify the server-startup pieces
quizDraft.prompt: Which two actions are part of starting this minimal local Express service?
quizDraft.hint: Choose the steps that create the application and make it listen locally.

help.concept: Express startup separates application creation from network listening.
help.hint_1: One action produces the object that owns routes.
help.hint_2: Another action binds that application to the provided local port.

options: Connect to a public API before defining routes.

quizDraft.title: Choose the response object
quizDraft.prompt: Complete the route-handler statement with the object used to send the HTTP response.
quizDraft.hint: The handler receives one object describing what came in and one object used to send data back.

help.concept: A route callback receives input through one argument and sends output through another.
help.hint_1: Focus on the argument used for outgoing data.
help.hint_2: The input-side argument is not the one used to send output.

quizDraft.template: Inside `(req, res) => { ... }`, the handler sends data through [blank1].

quizDraft.title: Put basic server setup in order
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange these conceptual steps from setup to a server that can answer the route.
quizDraft.hint: The application must exist before a route can be registered on it.

help.concept: Server setup has a dependency order: dependency, app, route, listener.
help.hint_1: Start with the dependency required to create the application.
help.hint_2: The listener is the final startup step after the route exists.
